caption:
OpenAI is retiring the ChatGPT Classic desktop app on January 30, 2027, and your chat history moves to the new app.
It also plans to merge the Chat and Work tabs into one ChatGPT, starting with a test for a small group of users.
Codex stays its own section.

Do you use the Work tab, or just chat?

paragraphs.text: OpenAI is retiring ChatGPT Classic, the original version of its desktop app, and plans to merge the Chat and Work tabs of its newer app into a single interface, 9to5Mac reported on November 2, 2026. A banner shown to Classic users says the app will retire on January 30, 2027, and that their full chat history will carry over to the new ChatGPT app.

Android Headlines reported the same plan, citing an email OpenAI sent to subscribers that was first reported by TechCrunch. According to that report, OpenAI will test the unified view with a small group of users before a wider rollout.
How the desktop app got here

In July 2026, OpenAI released a new desktop app that combined ChatGPT, Codex and Work, an agent mode for longer tasks, and renamed the original app ChatGPT Classic. 9to5Mac reported that critics objected to the switch from a native macOS app to an Electron-based one and found the new interface confusing, with some users struggling to find their chat history.

OpenAI later added a Chat and Work toggle at the top of the window and a sidebar menu for switching between ChatGPT and Codex. According to 9to5Mac, the Classic app was largely left untouched after that and became less useful as new features, such as selectable reasoning effort levels, arrived only in the new app.

In an interview with Joanna Stern published in late July, OpenAI president Greg Brockman agreed that the redesigned app was kind of a mess and said there should be no Work tab by the end of the year, with its functions folded into ChatGPT. He also said the company had hoped to launch the app with no tabs at all, and that Codex grew from 5 million to 10 million users in a few days after the change.

In its email, OpenAI said the combined design would let users move from exploring an idea to having ChatGPT carry it through in one place, 9to5Mac reported. Codex will remain a separate section of the desktop app.

The change comes alongside a shared usage allowance. Starting in December, Plus, Pro and Business subscribers will draw from one pool across ChatGPT and Codex instead of separate limits, and instant chats will not count against it, according to Android Headlines and 9to5Mac. OpenAI told users that more advanced models and complex tasks use more of the allowance, and that most users should not need to wait for resets more often than they do now. Subscribers can see their remaining usage and reset times in their account settings.

The plan reads as OpenAI conceding that splitting its desktop app into modes asked too much of ordinary users. Folding Work into the main chat window removes a choice most people did not want to make, while the shared allowance ties agent tasks and coding to the same budget as everyday chat. For people still on the Classic app, the January deadline means the switch is no longer optional.
Watch how quickly the combined Chat and Work view moves from the small test group to all desktop users, and whether OpenAI publishes the size of each plan's shared allowance before December.
